title: W8/S1 split — semantic prohibitions are not path globs
objective: Stop the compiler writing a natural-language prohibition into a field the Controller glob-matches against file paths, which makes do_not_build report PASS having enforced nothing. Separate semantic laws from filesystem globs across the compile/verify seam, and close the first of S1's four acceptance bullets.
success_criteria: A semantic prohibition never reaches the Controller as a path pattern: the compiler classifies each prohibition and only emits path_or_pattern when the statement is genuinely a repo path or glob.
The Controller's do_not_build gate matches only entries that supply a path pattern, and the substring fallback that treats a sentence as a path is gone.
No prohibition is dropped: semantic laws keep statement, rationale, source_refs and semantic_id, and stay visible in DO_NOT_BUILD.yaml under an explicit kind.
A test proves a semantic prohibition cannot make do_not_build FAIL by accident and cannot be silently counted as enforced.
A test proves a genuine path prohibition still trips do_not_build.
Full controller suite, PE conformance runner and the hardening suite stay green; no product behavior changes beyond the classification.

in: tests on both sides of the seam
out: The SemanticModel round-trip and semantic_diff — S1's other three acceptance bullets, a much larger build
S2 through S8, and W9/W10, which are sequenced behind them by dependency, not by a missing plan
compiler/synthesizer.py's parallel emission — read to confirm the same shape, changed only if the seam demands it
Any v3 surface, Program Lock, make campaign, or campaign activation
Merging PR #442 or any change to merge authority

todos.task: Add a prohibition classifier at the compiler seam: a statement that is a repo path or glob becomes path_or_pattern with kind=path; anything else becomes kind=semantic, carrying statement and rationale, with no path_or_pattern for the Controller to glob.
todos.shared_root_cause: One field carrying two kinds of thing, exactly as baseline_commit did in S0.

todos.task: Declare kind in the DO_NOT_BUILD schema so the distinction is contractual rather than incidental.
Make the Controller match only entries that supply a path pattern and remove the substring fallback that treats a sentence as a path. A gate must not appear to enforce what it cannot match.
todos.shared_root_cause: Same as B6: a gate reporting PASS having checked nothing.

todos.task: Tests both sides: a semantic prohibition cannot trip or be counted by do_not_build; a genuine path prohibition still trips it; the compiler classifies both shapes.
Regenerate manifests and update both trackers with the S1 partial and what S1 still needs.

milestones.outcome: Semantic laws and path globs travel in distinguishable channels.
milestones.unlocks: The Controller can enforce what it can actually match, and say nothing about what it cannot.

milestones.outcome: do_not_build no longer reports PASS on unenforceable input.
milestones.unlocks: S1's split bullet is closed and provable.

checkpoints.evidence_required: A semantic prohibition no longer reaches path_allowed; a path prohibition still does
checkpoints.no_go_action: If real campaigns depend on the substring fallback, stop and report rather than removing enforcement anyone relies on.

checkpoints.evidence_required: Controller suite, compile suite, conformance runner and hardening all green
checkpoints.no_go_action: Any regression: fix before publishing; do not push a red tree.

doc_root_surface_impact.reason: Narrative twin of the tracker; records the S1 partial.
No agent authority or command surface changes.
Generated digest; the edited files are covered.

disconfirming_questions: Does any real campaign rely on the substring fallback to enforce something today?
Is a prohibition statement ever legitimately a path, so classification would misroute it?
Does synthesizer.py emit the same shape, leaving the defect alive on a second path?
Does removing the fallback make do_not_build weaker rather than more honest?
assumed_false_ifs: If a shipped campaign's DO_NOT_BUILD entries are genuine globs already, T1's classifier must preserve them unchanged or it breaks live enforcement.
If the Controller's ContractError branch is load-bearing for directory-scope patterns, removing it would drop real matches.
stress_test.blast_radius: The compile seam and one Controller gate. Both are covered by existing suites (compile 649-test conformance runner, controller 112 tests). No runtime path outside verify changes; no schema field is removed, only added.
stress_test.rollback: git revert the slice commit. The schema change is additive and the classifier is deterministic, so reverting restores prior behavior exactly.

shared_causes: One field carrying two different kinds of thing — the same root cause as baseline_commit in S0.
A gate that cannot match its input still reporting PASS — the same root cause as B6.
deletions_or_consolidations: Removes the substring fallback rather than adding a second matcher beside it.

risks.risk: Removing the substring fallback drops enforcement someone relies on.
risks.mitigation: C1 checks live campaign artifacts before the removal lands; if any depend on it, stop and report.

risks.risk: A classifier misroutes a genuine glob as semantic, weakening enforcement.
risks.mitigation: Classify conservatively: anything that parses as a repo path or glob stays a path; only clearly non-path statements become semantic.

risks.risk: synthesizer.py carries the same emission and is left defective.
risks.mitigation: Read it in T1; bring it along if it shares the shape, and record it if it does not.

unknowns.question: Should an unenforceable semantic prohibition make do_not_build INCOMPLETE rather than PASS?
unknowns.decision_effect: Would change every campaign's gate output, not just this seam.
